attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his Substack post, summarising the commentary he collected.

semantics.note: The normalised wording keeps 'many people' and 'essentially the same' without adding anything. Supplying Sam Altman as the subject comes from context and is fair.

contract.note: The contract reads 'many' as a noticeable number of distinct commentators, not a majority, over May 1–22, 2024. That is an ordinary reading, and the speaker gave no threshold. The result depends on it.

evidence.note: Brian Merchant's commentary, dated May 21, 2024, is directly critical of Altman's conduct. One distinct author.
Geoffrey Miller's EA Forum essay, dated May 21, 2024, expresses strong distrust of Altman's leadership. A second distinct author with the same critical theme.
Dazed, May 22, 2024: Waite gives his own critical view and reports that many others raised similar concerns about Altman disregarding rules.

reviews.rationale: Three dated sources from distinct authors in the target window share a critical view of Altman's conduct and trustworthiness. Dazed also reports wider agreement among observers. The packet has no counterevidence suggesting the convergence was misrepresented. On the contract's plain reading of 'many', the observation holds.

attribution.note: Marcus's own opening lines in his Substack post.

semantics.note: It keeps the November comparison and limits the claim to 'the narrative', not measured public sentiment. 'Changed a lot' is preserved.

contract.note: Treating 'everybody' as rhetoric and 'the narrative' as prominent coverage is the ordinary reading and fair to the speaker. A literal reading would be stretched against him.

evidence.note: WIRED, Nov 20, 2023: about 95% of staff signed a letter demanding his return. This documents the prominent pro-Altman narrative in November.
TIME, May 21, 2024, reports an intense social-media backlash against Altman, showing a conspicuous critical turn.
The OpenAI board stated its distrust in November (company disclosure). This rules out literal unanimity but does not undo the support narrative that followed.
Microsoft's continued endorsement in May concerns the company, not Altman's standing. It limits any claim of universal abandonment, nothing more.

reviews.rationale: Dated coverage shows overwhelming visible support during the November reinstatement and an intense, publicly reported backlash by May 21, 2024. The board's November distrust and Microsoft's May partnership statements only limit literal or universal readings, which the plain reading does not require. The narrative did change substantially.
